findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022 — The empty Prisma update in `updateManyByCredentialId(..., {})` does not advance `@updatedAt`, leaving the selected-calendar cache timestamp stale after refresh.

[Medium/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller’s working directory instead of the script directory, so running from the repository root modifies or creates `.env` in the repository’s parent directory.

[Medium/api] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:72 — Delegated credentials are offered “Delete cached data” because `hasCache` ignores `delegationCredentialId`, but the endpoint rejects credentials not owned by the current user, guaranteeing an access-denied error.

[Low/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:87 — The cache timestamp is always formatted with `en-US`, displaying an incorrectly localized date for users of other locales.

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller’s working directory instead of the script directory, so running from the repository root modifies or creates `.env` in the repository’s parent directory.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that ENV_FILE="../.env" on line 5 of the new script uses a relative path that depends on the caller's working directory, not the script's location. If someone runs this script from the repository root (e.g., `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), the path `../` would resolve to the parent of the repository, not the parent of the scripts directory. This is a real bug that could cause the script to modify or create a .env file in an unintended location.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:72 — Delegated credentials are offered “Delete cached data” because `hasCache` ignores `delegationCredentialId`, but the endpoint rejects credentials not owned by the current user, guaranteeing an access-denied error.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx, `hasCache` is defined as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` (line 68), which doesn't consider `delegationCredentialId`. The `canDisconnect` check (line 67) does consider `delegationCredentialId`, but the cache deletion option only checks `hasCache`. So for a delegated credential with cache data, the 'Delete cached data' option would appear. In deleteCache.handler.ts (lines 17-22), the credential lookup requires `userId: user.id`, which would fail for delegated credentials not owned by the current user, resulting in 'Credential not found or access denied' error. This is a real UX bug where users see an option that will always fail.
